source: Khojasteh, Jiang, De Giorgis, van Harmelen, Ilievski (2026) Enhancing structural mapping with LLM-derived abstractions for analogical reasoning in narratives (YARN)
finding: Closest test of gap 1: an SME-style one-to-one mapping scorer fed by LLM-extracted event phrases and abstractions, versus the same LLM judging directly. On far analogies the mapping scorer beat the plain LLM only with abstraction, and only slightly. On near analogies it lost.
numbers: Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B. Mapping on raw event phrases (no abstraction): MCQ 0.17 (chance 0.25); ARN far 0.24 for Qwen. Best abstraction: MCQ 0.46 vs best LLM-only 0.41 (Qwen), 0.45 vs 0.28 (Llama). ARN far: Llama mapping 0.46 vs zero-shot 0.42; Qwen mapping 0.47 vs zero-shot 0.52. ARN near: Qwen CoT 0.79 vs mapping 0.69; Llama zero-shot 0.73 to 0.76 vs mapping lower.
quote: adding abstractions substantially improves performance, yielding results competitive with LLM event mapping
limits: Small 8B models only. Mapping is cosine similarity between phrase embeddings with a FAME-style one-to-one assignment, not a higher-order trickle-down score, so it does not test systematicity itself. No token-cost comparison. Far-near cases stay below the 0.5 random line (0.41 Qwen, 0.42 Llama) in every setting.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 is only partly answered: structure-style scoring plus abstraction is competitive on far items at 8B scale, not clearly better, and worse on near items. Use it when surface lures are likely, and put the abstraction step before the score.

source: Khojasteh et al. (2026) YARN - effect of abstraction level and input format
finding: The abstraction level that works depends on how much surface overlap the pair has. Low-level abstraction helps near analogies; higher-level abstraction with modifiers removed helps the hard far-near cases. Input format and the mapping instruction change accuracy, sometimes sharply.
numbers: Qwen far-near best 0.41 (Acon,1 root only), Llama 0.42; both below the 0.50 random baseline in all settings. Far-far best 0.56 (Qwen) and 0.58 (Llama). Qwen zero-shot ARN near with sentences 0.88 vs 0.52 after switching the event-mapping instruction. Qwen zero-shot MCQ 0.44 with one input format vs 0.38 with event phrases. NLI scorer in a pilot reached 0.6.
limits: Authors list extraction and abstraction errors, missing causal links, and surface-bound mapping as open problems. Error cost was not isolated as a number.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 4: extraction quality and abstraction level matter more than the scorer. Re-representation helps surface-rich pairs only when it strips surface cues, and no single level works everywhere, so the agent should try two levels and compare.

source: Ye, Wang, Choi, et al. (2024) AnaloBench: benchmarking the identification of abstract and long-context analogies (EMNLP 2024)
finding: Story analogy selection gets harder for models as stories get longer (more surface detail around the same relation). Scale stops helping on long stories. Retrieval of analogous stories from a 200-story bank is near random for long stories.
numbers: T1 4-way choice (random 25%). GPT-4: 89.1% (1 sentence), 66.5% (10), 60.7% (30). Human: 96.0, 72.5, 73.3. Gap 6.9 points at 1 sentence and 28.8 at 30 sentences (paper text). GPT-3.5: 65.3, 46.4, 30.8. T2 retrieval from 200 stories, GPT-4 Turbo recall@3: 42.9% (1 sentence), 6.5% (10), 3.9% (30), random 1.6%. Claude-v2: 10.2, 5.3, 5.4.
limits: The same analogy is told at different lengths, so length is a proxy for bottom-heaviness, not a direct test of a systematicity scorer. 2023-era models. Human annotations only for T1.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 proxy: adding surface detail to a fixed relational core hurts LLMs far more than people. Supports a compress-to-relations step before comparing or retrieving long cases.

source: Hope, Chan, Kittur, Shahaf (2017) Accelerating innovation through analogy mining (KDD)
finding: Retrieval by a learned relational summary (purpose and mechanism vectors) finds analogies better than surface text methods, and the retrieved cases led people to better ideas. A direct test of retrieval by relational summary versus surface text (gap 9).
numbers: Precision at top 1%: purpose-only 0.739, mechanism-only 0.696, TF-IDF 0.63, LSA 0.413 (recall about 0.02 at 1%). Ideation study, 38 AMT workers, within-subject, 749 ideas. P(good idea), k=2 judges: analogy condition 0.71 vs TF-IDF 0.28 vs random 0.27; k=3: 0.56 vs 0.16 vs 0.14 (p<.01). Over the 9 shared seeds: 46% vs TF-IDF 30% vs random 37%. Judge Fleiss kappa 0.51.
limits: Weak structure only (two slots), product text, crowd labels where surface-only pairs were marked as analogies, which favours the baselines. Confidence intervals wide (k=2 CI 0.48 to 0.87). Pre-LLM.
agent_relevance: Partial yes for gap 9. A relational summary (what it is for, how it works) used as the index closes much of the surface-recall gap. The agent can store each case with a short purpose and mechanism line and retrieve on that.

source: RA-RFT authors (2026) Learning to reason by analogy via retrieval-augmented reinforcement fine-tuning
finding: Retrieving worked examples by reasoning usefulness beats retrieving by embedding similarity. An off-the-shelf semantic retriever was barely better than a random trace from the same problem type.
numbers: Qwen3-1.7B after RA-RFT, mean over AIME24, AIME25, HMMT25, BrUMO25 (average@32): random trace 37.6; Qwen3-Embedding-4B 38.5; Reason-ModernColBERT 40.7; fine-tuned embedding 40.5; fine-tuned Reason-ModernColBERT 47.4. Retriever recall@1 against gold labels: 2.3% off-the-shelf, 43.5% fine-tuned. RA-SFT 40.5 vs SFT 39.7.
limits: Trains both retriever and model, so it is not a prompt-only scaffold. Math problems, not narrative analogies. Relevance is learned, not computed from structure. One model size for the ablation. Author names not recorded.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: surface-similarity retrieval is close to random for reasoning transfer. A retrieval key based on solution structure is needed. We cannot train, but the agent can approximate with a relational-summary key.

source: Authors not recorded (2025) Can LLMs help improve analogical reasoning for strategic decisions? Experimental evidence from humans and GPT-4
finding: In a Gick-and-Holyoak style matching task with two source stories, GPT-4 found every relevant source when hinted but also accepted wrong ones based on surface match. Humans were precise but missed most. Matching (judging which analogy is right) is its own step that needs causal mapping.
numbers: Humans n=199, GPT-4 n=60 runs. No hint: GPT-4 never claimed the correct story (precision 0, recall 0, accuracy 0.50 to 0.54); humans precision 0.42 and 1.00, recall 0.06 and 0.22. With hint: GPT-4 recall 1.00, precision 0.52 and 0.50, F1 0.67 to 0.68, accuracy 0.50 to 0.53; humans precision 0.67 to 0.75, recall 0.26 to 0.39, F1 0.38 to 0.51, accuracy 0.57 to 0.63.
limits: Business-strategy problems; GPT-4 only; human sample is business-school undergraduates. One study.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 6: a plain LLM judge is high recall and low precision when surface cues mislead. A separate verify-the-mapping step aimed at precision (check that the causal chain lines up) is the missing piece, and its cost should be tested.

source: ARCANA authors (2026) ARCANA: a benchmark for abstraction and analogical reasoning
finding: Frontier 2025-26 models (GPT 5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus 4.5, Grok 4.1 Fast) still fall below undergraduates on far analogies from real-world objects to abstract grid transforms. Getting the analogy right was a bottleneck.
numbers: 200 tasks. Total solved (union of setups, pass@3 across 12 attempts): GPT 5.2 51.20% with typos counted / 48.33% without; Gemini 3 Pro 43.06% / 29.19%; Grok 4.1 Fast 24.88% / 18.66%; Claude Opus 4.5 8.61% / 7.18%. Humans pass@1 68.96% / 58.35%; tasks solved by 2 or more humans 93.5% / 96%; 1,659 human answers. Paired bootstrap: best LLM still 10.13 points below humans strict, 17.67 typo-tolerant. Pulley category: Gemini 100% analogy correctness, GPT 0%. ConceptSIR solves 9 of 17 hard tasks in 2.22 loops on average.
limits: Different task from ARN (grid output). Default reasoning settings via OpenRouter; thinking budget not varied. LLM figure is best of many attempts, human figure is one attempt, so the true gap is likely larger. Authors' own method and one undergraduate sample.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partly answered: current top models still fail a share of far analogies. More attempts raise accuracy but do not close it. An explicit slippage-and-reflect loop helps on a subset, a case for a mapping-check step.

source: Bowdle and Gentner (1997) Informativity and asymmetry in comparisons, Cognitive Psychology 34
finding: People prefer the more systematic (causally coherent) passage as the base of a comparison, and they project more inferences from base to target in that direction. Asymmetry needs alignable structure and tracks systematicity, not the size of distinctive feature sets.
numbers: Exp 1 (N=48 undergraduates, 18 story pairs): forward comparisons M=.76 (deletion .68, replacement .79, shuffled .81), t(47)=10.52. Exp 4 (N=48): forward inferences M=.80 (deletion .85, replacement .83, shuffled .73). Projected inferences standard-to-variant .81 vs .24 reverse (deletion), .71 vs .28 (replacement). Exp 5 projected modifications .86 vs .47 (deletion). Alignability ratings from 48 more students: 5.29, 5.09, 4.09 (7-point).
quote: asymmetries can therefore be predicted from the relative degree of systematicity or conceptual coherence
limits: Same lab as Clement and Gentner; student samples; stories built by deleting or replacing causal links. Experiments 2, 3 and 6 not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: use the richer, more causally connected case as the base and project inferences from it to the poorer one. The reverse direction projects less. Same-lab evidence only.

source: Authors not recorded (2026) When models know more than they say: probing analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Narrative analogies are weakly encoded and weakly prompted in small open models; rhetorical parallelism is decodable by a probe but not by a prompt. Frontier closed models prompt well on both.
numbers: Prompting MAP / MRR / pairwise accuracy: Claude Opus 0.8158 / 0.9127 / 0.8892 and GPT-5.2 0.8181 / 0.9126 / 0.8921 on one task; Llama-1B 0.3486 / 0.4487 / 0.4937; Llama-8B 0.2987 / 0.3540 / 0.4512. Second task: Claude 0.9084 / 0.9077 / 0.9558, GPT-5.2 0.9000 / 0.9009 / 0.9753, Llama 0.1779 / 0.1921 / 0.4658 and 0.1710 / 0.1819 / 0.4760. Llama-1B rhetorical probe MAP 0.93 vs 0.18 prompted.
limits: Row-to-task assignment in the extracted table text is uncertain. Ranking tasks, not forced-choice far-near. Not a systematicity test.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 side evidence: closed frontier models rank analogous pairs well in this ranking format; the weakness is in small open models. Do not assume ARN-style failure for the agent's own model without testing it.

source: Authors not recorded (2025) The curious case of analogies: investigating analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Inside open models, correct story analogies show strong structural alignment between source and target tokens; failures show degraded or misplaced alignment. Relational information is often present in mid-upper layers but not applied to the new entities.
numbers: Patching hidden states fixed up to 38.4% of wrong proportional-analogy cases and led to revised answers in up to 38.1% (Llama-2-13B +32.3 and +25.9, Gemma-7B +38.4 and +38.1, Qwen2.5-14B +35.6 and +30.5, column meaning partly unclear). Linear probe accuracy up to 82.9% in mid layers.
limits: Open 2023-24 models. Patching is not available to a prompt-only agent. Only the PDF text was skimmed, not every table.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 7: alignment quality predicts success inside the model, which supports writing the mapping out and checking it. The relation is often known but unused.

source: Sourati, Ilievski, Sommerauer, Jiang (2024) ARN - abstract re-read for gap 7
finding: Abstract page re-read. The paper tests zero-shot, solved examples and chain-of-thought; GPT-4 scored below random zero-shot on far analogies. It has no reasoning-model (o1, o3, R1) results.
numbers: Abstract: GPT4.0 'below random' on far analogies; best few-shot model 'halfway between random and humans'.
limits: Only the abstract was re-read; numbers in a26, b24 and c15 stand. I found no later paper that reruns ARN on reasoning models, but my search tools were rate-limited, so absence is not proven.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: no direct ARN retest with reasoning models found. YARN (d01) and ARCANA (d07) are the nearest, and both still show failures.

source: Jiayang et al. (2023) StoryAnalogy - abstract re-read
finding: Analogy identification in a 24K story-pair corpus is very hard for sentence embeddings and LLMs; ChatGPT scored about 30% on multiple choice versus over 85% for humans.
limits: Abstract only. Already counted in K17.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 background: plain LLM judging at 2023 level was near chance on story analogy with confounds. Newer models need retesting.

source: Search record 2026-10-31: independent replication of Clement and Gentner 1991 (gap 2)
finding: Searched Crossref, Europe PMC and arXiv listings for an independent-lab replication, effect sizes or expert samples. Found none. Independent work exists on related questions (Lee and Holyoak 2007, already a19 and a20) but not a direct replication.
numbers: 0 direct replications found. Within-lab extensions: Bowdle and Gentner 1997 (d08).
limits: The web search quota was used up and OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar returned 429, so the search was incomplete. This is absence of evidence only.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open. Treat systematicity-as-selection as single-lab and do not claim a replication rate.

source: Search record 2026-10-31: Lee and Holyoak dissociation in LLMs (gap 5) and token cost versus best-of-N (gap 10)
finding: No paper found that tests the similarity-versus-inference-strength dissociation in LLMs, and none that costs an explicit mapping-score step against best-of-N. YARN (d01) used only 8B models and reports no token counts.
limits: The arXiv search interface was rate-limited after the first batch of queries, so papers may be hidden.
agent_relevance: Gaps 5 and 10 stay open and are candidates for our own test: run both judgments on causal-preventer items and count tokens.

source: Khojasteh et al. (2026) YARN - extraction recipe (gap 3)
finding: Extraction used: split each story into atomic events with a temporal index, then give each event an open-vocabulary frame '[modifier]-[root]'. The authors chose LLM frames over FrameNet and semantic parsers because those could not give context-dependent narrative abstractions.
numbers: Models: Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B. Abstraction types: conceptual (two hierarchy levels), evaluative, stage, narrative arc. Best MCQ combination: conceptual plus evaluative constraint (Qwen 0.46, Llama 0.45) vs 0.17 and 0.16 without abstraction.
limits: No extraction-precision metric against gold relations is reported, so the cost of extraction error is not quantified.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: a usable extraction recipe exists (events, then frames, then roles). How much error costs the score is still unmeasured.
